observation.visible_scene: A wide twilight sky with a soft blue gradient, streaked by pink-and-orange lit altocumulus clouds forming a diagonal band from the upper-left toward the center and a larger cloud mass on the right. A thin dark horizon line at the bottom shows a faint city-skyline silhouette and low hills. The camera is fixed and the overall composition stays constant throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The cloud formations, their pink illumination, and the horizon skyline show no detectable translation, expansion, or deformation between the first and last frames; the scene is effectively static over this ~2.7 s window.

A few tiny dark specks (consistent with distant birds) appear at different positions in different frames (e.g. near the upper-left, mid-right, and lower-left cloud regions at various times), indicating small moving points crossing the sky rather than a single tracked object.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident: the horizon and cloud edges hold the same pixel positions across frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the clouds drift at all over a longer timescale (too slow to register here).
The identity, number, and flight paths of the tiny specks, and whether they enter or leave the frame outside this segment.
The sun position / cause of the pink lighting and any change in light color beyond this excerpt.
uncertain_details: The moving specks are too small to confirm as birds versus sensor/dust artifacts; their trajectories cannot be reliably linked across frames.
Any minute cloud motion is below the resolution of these samples, so 'static' describes only what is visible here.
